Apple Pay is the go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in physical stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more powerful—here's how they work.

iOS 27 New Design

Among the many changes in iOS 27, one of my favorites is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier for users to switch between different credit cards when checking out on websites and apps.

With the new design, you can swipe left or right directly on the main Apple Pay checkout page to switch between different credit cards, or tap on a credit card to view a grid list of all available Apple Pay credit cards.

The new design also makes it easier to view information for individual credit cards, including rewards, balances, buy-now-pay-later options, and more.

iOS 27 is currently available to developers and public beta users, with an official launch expected this fall.

Amex Rewards Points

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that will allow users to pay with Amex Rewards Points.

When using an Amex card to shop online or in apps, in addition to displaying your membership rewards points balance, a new "Use Rewards Points" option will be added. You can use points to pay for all or part of your purchase during the Apple Pay checkout process.

Amex points redeemed through Apple Pay are worth 0.7 cents each. In other words, 10,000 points can be converted into US$70 to use toward purchases.

Tap to Share

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new "Tap to Share" feature to use with Apple Pay in physical stores.

Apple says this feature, coming this fall, is an extension of "Tap to Pay on iPhone." Apple explains:

Customers can simply tap to connect to a participating merchant's iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store shopping experience, and can securely share email addresses, other contact information, shipping addresses, membership rewards information, and more. Customers can also view the items in their shopping cart in real time to keep track of what has been purchased and to make sure all discounts and promotions have been applied correctly.

Once done, customers can use Apple Pay to complete checkout on their own iPhone.

Topping Up Debit Cards

Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage their debit card balances directly within the Apple Pay interface.

According to Apple, you can top up supported debit cards using Apple Pay within Apple Wallet or at checkout.

Conclusion

As Apple Pay becomes increasingly popular among retailers, it's great to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. Personally, whether I'm shopping online or in a physical store, Apple Pay is my preferred payment method.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favorite Apple Pay features? Let us know in the comments.
